## Design

### 2026-10-08 – First entry,

**0.75h**

First entry,

Started on the pcb design with creating the project. After that started on the schematic design. Picked all the components that i would need finding them from LCSC and JLC. Added the main IC, the LED's, the battery holder, the button and the resistors. After that started on the wiring. First the LED matrix, to use less pins wired it with a multiplexed layout. Continued with the power circuitry and added all of the capacitors. Looked at the main IC datasheet to make sure that all was connected correctly and that is it!

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/bef5b4a4-54c7-418e-af5a-797787bb5942/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-10 – Second entry,

**2.43h**

Second entry,

Started with connecting all of the CH32V003 pins. First the LED's then the button and finally the Programming Pins. Added one extra capacitor and a switch to turn the thing off, then converted to PCB.

Started with the LED's. First arranged them in a matrix and made sure that they were correctly aligned. Then turned all of them by 45 degrees and made sure that each of the rows and the columns had a 4mm spacing in between them. After that arranged my board settings by setting the board layer count to 4 and tweaking some DRC rules. After that created the board outline according to the led matrix and started to route the top part of the led matrix. After that placed all of the components in their place. Wired up the column resistors and tried to fit everything. Modified the footprint of the battery holder to make it fit and modified the proggramming pin footprint to make the pads one sided. After that rewired the resistors and realised that all of the components will not fit if the layout stays like this. That is it!

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/824e1d6c-5e89-4a28-901d-c8f287b14229/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-11 – Third entry,

**2.77h**

Third entry,

Started by adding mounting holes for the brooch needle. After that repositioned the ch32v003 and started to route the tracks. First the matrix columns and then the matrix rows. Next wired up the power side of the board, the power switch the capacitors and the battery holder. After that made sure that the LED's are centered, fixed the battery holder footprint and looked at jlcpcb capabilities. Added some text and correctly placed the designators. Checked DRC and made the pcb corners curved. Found the needed components locally and added them to the bom. Added some more text and a version label.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/eb23a862-4184-4090-b12b-72e1a93a4cf3/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-11 – Fourth entry,

**0.25h**

Fourth entry,

Started by better laying out the schematic. After that checked DRC and exported all the necessary PCB files ( aka the GERBER the BOM and the Pick and Place). After that exported the Schematic and a couple of pictures of the PCB. Ended the time lapse by exporting the EasyEDA project files.
